title: Windowed amortizer for tenant crediting and late-arrival fixes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The existing billing pipeline produces incorrect tenant credit application when usage events arrive out-of-order or are duplicated across ingestion shards. This results in temporary overcharges followed by expensive backfill reconciles. Goal: implement a streaming, windowed amortizer service that applies tenant credits and discounts across bounded time windows with explicit late-arrival correction and safe shadow-apply semantics. The service will be shard-aware, idempotent, and compatible with existing ledger schema so we can gradually switch traffic with feature flags. Key constraints: low-latency charging (median additional latency <10ms per request for hot paths), bounded memory footprint per shard, ability to backfill windows deterministically, and full audit trail to support invoice adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: New amortizer computes credit adjustments per tenant per 1-minute tumbling window and writes a single consolidated credit record per window
Late-arriving events up to 24 hours are corrected via window re-emit and a compensating entry; customers see at most one corrected invoice cycle
System can be enabled via runtime feature flag for a subset of tenants and fall back to current billing path without data loss
End-to-end test harness validates deterministic output for randomized out-of-order event sequences
Telemetry: per-tenant error rate <0.1% and applied-credit variance within 0.5% of batch recompute baseline for sampled tenants
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Windowing model: chosen tumbling windows (1m) vs sliding because tumbling simplifies idempotent merge and reduces double-count risk on replays
State store: use CockroachDB materialized table keyed by (tenant_id, window_start, shard_id) for durability and easy ad-hoc queries; tradeoff is slightly higher write latency vs RocksDB local state

Late-arrival policy: 24-hour correction horizon with tombstone-based re-emits. Longer horizons increase complexity and storage costs; 24h covers most cross-region ingestion lag seen in traffic profiles
Merge semantics: use monotonic sequence numbers from ingress to detect duplicates and a deterministic merge order to ensure convergent results
Backfill strategy: provide deterministic batch recompute job for windows >24h (cold path) instead of keeping unbounded streaming reprocessing
implementation_steps: 1) Spec API and schema changes for amortized credit record (contrib column list in design doc)
2) Implement windowing library in streaming runtime (shared util) with watermark advancement and per-shard checkpointing
3) Materialize per-window intermediate state in CRDB and expose read APIs for console/debugging
4) Implement compensating-credit write logic with idempotency token and shadow-apply mode
5) Add end-to-end tests (chaos shuffled ingestion, delayed events) and unit tests for merge behavior
6) Integrate observability (per-window latency, late-arrival histogram, correction counts) and dashboard
7) Rollout: start with 1% of tenants in shadow-apply for 48h, then 5%, 25%, 100% with monitoring gates
8) Post-rollout: enable auto-backfill monitor and schedule incremental batch recompute for legacy windows
progress_updates: 2025-01-10: Design doc v0 posted (Confluence). High-level API and schema sketched. (owner: Aisha)
2025-01-15: Proof-of-concept windowing util implemented in streaming runtime; local integration tests pass for single-shard replay. (owner: Liang)
2025-01-22: Chose CRDB materialized state over local RocksDB after perf eval — write latency increase measured but acceptable under amortizer SLOs. (decision recorded)
2025-01-28: Compensating-entry semantics implemented with idempotency keys; added shadow-apply flag to control writes to billing ledger
2025-02-01: End-to-end randomized chaos tests added — initial runs show deterministic convergence for 98% of cases, remaining failures traced to rare clock skew handling
2025-02-04: Mitigation for clock skew applied: ingest timestamps normalized to tenant timezone window; pushed patch to POC branch
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High write amplification to CRDB during peak; Mitigation: batch writes per-window and backpressure to ingest gateway
Risk: Customer confusion from corrected invoices; Mitigation: generate human-readable auditable explanation log and plan communication through billing team
Risk: Edge-case duplicates across shard boundaries; Mitigation: enforce cross-shard monotonic seq numbers at ingress and add duplicate detector
Risk: Observability blind spots; Mitigation: add sampling-based golden-tenant comparison to batch recompute baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests for window open/close, merge ordering, tombstone handling
Property tests: randomized event ordering with deterministic final state assertion against single-threaded batch recompute
Integration tests: deploy to staging with CRDB and run 72h ingestion replay from recent real traffic (anonymized)
Canary plan: enable shadow-apply for 1% tenants and compare outputs to legacy path for 24h before enabling write path
Load test: synthetic peak QPS with 10k tenants to validate memory and CRDB write QPS
rollout_plan: Shadow-apply 5% for 48h and validate correction counts and telemetry
Enable write path for 5% tenants behind feature flag and monitor for 7 days
Gradual increase to 25% and 100% with automated rollback on correction-rate or latency SLO breach
Decommission legacy path incrementally after 90 days post 100% rollout and successful audit
observability_requirements: Metric: late_arrival_latency histogram (ms), percentile 99 < 20000 for 99% windows
Trace: end-to-end trace across ingest -> amortizer -> ledger write with span tags for window_id and shard_id
Dashboard: sample-tenant diff feed comparing amortizer output vs batch recompute baseline
